thread.title: United Nations to Cut 25% of its Global Peacekeeping Force in Response to US Funding Strains
thread.title_full: United Nations to Cut 25% of its Global Peacekeeping Force in Response to US Funding Strains

author: Associated Press Television News
title: United Nations to Cut 25% of its Global Peacekeeping Force in Response to US Funding Strains
text:
• The United Nations will reduce its peacekeeping force by 25%, equating to approximately 13,000-14,000 troops.
• This decision is a response to funding cuts from the United States, the largest donor to the U.N.
• The U.N. plans to cut its peacekeeping budget by approximately 15% for the current year.
• The reduction will affect over 50,000 peacekeepers deployed across nine global missions.
• Countries with U.N. peacekeeping missions include Congo, Central African Republic, South Sudan, Lebanon, Cyprus, and Kosovo.
• U.N. Secretary General Antonio Guterres emphasized that U.N. peacekeeping is a cost-effective tool for international peace and security.
• The decision followed a meeting between Guterres and representatives from major donor countries, including U.S. ambassador Mike Waltz.
• Waltz stated that the U.S. aims to reassess the effectiveness of U.N. agencies and programs before making further contributions.
• U.N. peacekeeping operations have increased from 11,000 personnel at the end of the Cold War to around 52,000 currently.
• The U.S. will commit $680 million to nine peacekeeping efforts, down from $1 billion the previous year.
• Contributions from the U.S. and China account for half of the U.N.'s peacekeeping budget.
• China has indicated it will fulfill its full contribution by the end of the year.
